canonical_title: Stall and loss of control warning

versions.title_at_revision: Stall and loss of control warning
versions.text:
Standard: Warning or indication of approach to stall or to departure from controlled flight are clear and unambiguous, and the onset of stall warning occurs within the speed and lift range as specified in MIL-STD-1797, Stall Approach paragraph. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Analysis.
(1) Conduct analysis and simulation to assess the timeliness and appropriateness of warning and indication of approach to stall or loss of air vehicle control as specified in MIL-STD-1797, Warning Cues paragraph, Stall Approach paragraph, Stall Warning paragraph, Uncommanded Oscillations prior to Stall paragraph, Cockpit Controls prior to Stall paragraph, and Departure Warning paragraph, for each combination of regions of handling qualities, air vehicle states, flight phases, and environmental conditions. Test.
  (1) Lab test: Conduct piloted simulation and evaluation to assess the timeliness and appropriateness of warning and indication of approach to stall or loss of air vehicle control as specified in MIL-STD-1797, Warning Cues paragraph, Stall Approach paragraph, Stall Warning paragraph, Uncommanded Oscillations prior to Stall paragraph, Cockpit Controls prior to Stall paragraph, and Departure Warning paragraph, for each combination of regions of handling qualities, air vehicle states, flight phases, and environmental conditions. Prior to entering operational test/operations, verify the standard by the above and following method(s): Test.
  (2) Flight test: Conduct flight test to assess the timeliness and appropriateness of warning and indication of approach to stall or loss of air vehicle control as specified in MIL-STD-1797, Warning Cues paragraph, Stall Approach paragraph, Stall Warning paragraph, Uncommanded Oscillations prior to Stall paragraph, Cockpit Controls prior to Stall paragraph, and Departure Warning paragraph, for selected combinations of regions of handling qualities, air vehicle states, flight phases, and environmental conditions.
